Keywords: Vladimir grand prince and khanly recognition
RagShortTexts: Alexander acquired the grand principality of Vladimir in 1252.
Khanly recognition still requires local collection and cooperation.

Variants.Content: Alexander has held Vladimir’s grand principality since 1252. Recognition at the khan’s court matters in princely rivalry. A visit requires attendants and gifts and brings demands for revenue; cities, retainers and local elites must still cooperate after a title is obtained.
Escorting a prince to the khan requires guarding gifts, animals and attendants while leaving home. News of recognition does not replace specific garrison orders or supplies.
Khanly recognition strengthens a claim against rivals but does not transport tribute. Allocation of gifts, accounts and shortfalls determines whether urban cooperation with the grand prince lasts.
Court journeys draw on local animals, food and revenue. Townspeople ask what demands envoys bring back; households need delivery dates alongside existing local dues.
